tasks.author: ai-task-writer-h
tasks.prompt: Explain in a short paragraph how the parser decides which encoding to read a Python source file with, including what happens when no declaration is given and the cases that end in an error.

rubric.text: Without a declaration or UTF-8 signature the file is read as UTF-8 from Python 3.0 on (ASCII was the earlier default), not ASCII today.
The magic comment only counts on line 1 or 2 and must match the coding[:=] pattern; if line 1 matches, line 2 is ignored.
A UTF-8 signature (BOM) means utf-8 even without a comment, and a BOM plus a comment naming any encoding other than utf-8 is an error.
An encoding name unknown to Python raises an error during compilation.
Encodings that use two or more bytes for every character, such as UTF-16, are not accepted as source encodings.

tasks.notes: cross-section: Defining the Encoding, Concepts and Phases.
